criteria.note: README.md documents the tracker integration as a first-class shipped capability: a new bullet in 'What the plugin ships' next to the fleet bullet, describing both directions truthfully. The MIRROR is stated one-way and event-driven (a spec's status plus a closing comment on its child issue, a plan's work graph onto an epic and child issues, reconciled from the event stream, never polled, repository the single source of truth). INTAKE is the other direction (a Jira ticket or a structured Confluence requirements page becomes a routing-resolved WARP spec draft, source linked, content treated as data). No operating metric and no credential appear in the README bullet; it defers 'how to turn it on' to docs/plugin.md.

docs/plugin.md new section 12.2 tells an adopter how to turn it on with four pieces, all real: the per-org .warp/trackers.json config (warp.tracker/v1, routing by label/component/field plus the WARP-status to tracker-status status_map, template at plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json which exists); the OPTIONAL tracker_repo front-matter field on specs and plans (check_tracker_repo in .warp/validate.py, enforced parallel to the lane fields, fails closed on an unknown repo when a config is wired); auth by reference not secret (token_ref e.g. env:JIRA_TOKEN, fails closed, raw credential never in a file/prompt/proof/log); and the Confluence requirements template at plugin/templates/confluence-requirements-template.md which exists.

Every named thing exists in the shipped engine: modules .warp/tracker.py, .warp/validate.py, .warp/tracker_adapter.py, .warp/tracker_mirror.py, .warp/tracker_intake.py, .warp/tracker_conformance.py; classes JiraCloudAdapter (tracker_intake.py:297) and ConfluenceCloudAdapter (tracker_intake.py:408); the FakeTracker (tracker_adapter.py:205); the five spec events (spec.ready, spec.blocked, verdict.recorded, spec.shipped, merge.completed) and four plan events (plan.created, plan.approved, plan.revised, work.pulled) all present in tracker_mirror.py; the intake_source field and the /warp:intake skill (plugin/skills/intake). The mechanical-versus-reference split matches capabilities.yaml exactly: routing, seam, spec mirror, epic mirror, intake logic, conformance are mechanical (gate-tested offline against the FakeTracker); the live JiraCloudAdapter and ConfluenceCloudAdapter are reference (wired per repo, need a live instance, not run in the gate). The not-yet-live edges are stated as such rather than implied complete: epic/child creation against live Jira is 'wired in a later increment' (matches jira_cloud_intake_adapter) and the Confluence adapter reads pages and posts comments only, no status workflow (matches confluence_cloud_intake_adapter). No over-claim of turnkey live integration.

docs/plugin.md section 12.4 states both governing principles: the mirror is one-way and the repository wins if the index and the tracker disagree, consistent with the standing 'do not recreate a tracker in Markdown' rule (an answer that changes a requirement is committed to the spec, not left in a ticket comment); and tracker content is untrusted input, never instructions (a ticket or page is data, sanitized against front-matter injection via _fm_safe, linked as a source, never executed). Both directions are also restated as one-way and never-polling in the section intro.

findings.text: Non-blocking, out of scope. The shipped plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json uses token_ref 'secrets:jira_token' as its example, but the default resolver in tracker_intake.py only strips an 'env:' prefix and otherwise reads os.environ.get(<literal>), so 'secrets:jira_token' would not resolve and fails closed. The WARP-0610 docs are true here: they use env:JIRA_TOKEN and state the default resolver reads the named environment variable, and never claim the secrets: template example works. The template value is a pre-existing nit separate from this docs spec; noted for the record only.

Non-blocking, out of scope. The module-header comment in .warp/tracker_intake.py summarizes the Jira adapter signature as 'JiraCloudAdapter(base_url, token_ref)' while the real constructor is __init__(self, base_url, email, token_ref, ...). This is an internal code comment, not part of the WARP-0610 docs, and does not affect any WARP-0610 claim.
